description: Signed mandates v0 (draft), SPEC-v0.md section 7. Each case: a compact JWS, the JWK Set the verifier trusts for the issuer, and whether the signed mandate is accepted. The verifier under test counts as hm-verifier:conf-0001, the audience of the cases (SPEC-v0 section 7.1). The keys are test keys; their private parts are in conformance/keys/test-keys.private.json.

cases.why: mandate with audience and expires signed with EdDSA by a key trusted for its issuer
mandate signed with ES256
payload changed after signing
signature removed
payload detached
algorithm none
signed over a form that is not canonical: one mandate has exactly one signed form
the keys are trusted for another issuer than the one the mandate names
mandate without issuer and version
valid signature over an invalid mandate
key ID that the verifier does not know
ES256 signature with the higher of the two possible values of s: only the lower one is accepted
line feed inside the payload segment: base64url without any other character
line feed inside the signature segment
padding on the payload segment
header member names in upper case, correctly signed: names are case-sensitive
additional header member typ, correctly signed: exactly alg and kid
header member crit, correctly signed
EdDSA signature whose S is S + L of the valid signature: a signature has exactly one form, S is less than L (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.7)
header alg ES256 with the kid of an Ed25519 key, signed with that key: alg must match the key type (7.1)
EdDSA signature whose R is the identity encoded non-canonically (y = p + 1) with a matching S: a verifier accepts only canonical encodings of R (7.1)
correctly signed valid mandate without audience: a signed mandate names the verifier it is for (7.1)
correctly signed valid mandate without expires: a signed mandate expires (7.1)
correctly signed mandate with a noncharacter in its name: not I-JSON (3.1 no. 1), and displayed text (3.1 no. 8) excludes it as well; a correction does not apply to mandates (14)
signed with a key that the key set names only under the member X: member names of a JWK are case-sensitive, so X is an unknown member (7.1, RFC 7517)
the same key set and a signature by the key under x: X is ignored as an unknown member, not an error (7.1, RFC 7517 section 4)
signed with a key that the key set names only under the member KEYS (7.1)
the key set names the kid of the signature only under the member KID (7.1)
the key type is RSA; OKP appears only under the member KTY (7.1)
a key set whose member names are all in upper case has no keys (7.1, 10.2)
a line feed in x: base64url has no line breaks (7.1)
the member d with an empty value: a key with d is a private key, whatever its value (7.1, RFC 8037 section 2)
the member d with the value null (7.1, RFC 8037 section 2)
public key of small order, the identity: the signature with S = 0 verifies for every message, so such a key is rejected (7.1)
public key of small order, order 8: the signature verifies for every message of its class, so such a key is rejected (7.1)
signed with an Ed25519 key that also carries y: y is not a member of an OKP key, so it is an unknown member and ignored (7.1, RFC 7517 section 4)
signed with a key whose use is sig (7.1, RFC 7517 section 4.2)
the only key is meant for encryption (use enc): it cannot be used, so the key set verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2, RFC 7517 section 4.2)
signed with a key whose key_ops contain verify (7.1, RFC 7517 section 4.3)
the only key may only sign (key_ops without verify): it cannot be used to verify (7.1, 10.2, RFC 7517 section 4.3)
signed with an Ed25519 key whose alg is EdDSA, the algorithm of its type (7.1, RFC 7517 section 4.4)
an Ed25519 key whose alg is ES256: an algorithm that does not fit its type, so it cannot be used (7.1, 10.2, RFC 7517 section 4.4)
a protected header of 256 bytes after decoding, white space included: the limit (7.1)
a protected header of 257 bytes after decoding: longer than 256 bytes (7.1)
an Ed25519 key of mixed order (a key plus a point of order 8) is a key, and this signature holds without the cofactor: its k is a multiple of 8 (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.7)
the same key of mixed order, a signature whose k is not a multiple of 8: it holds only with the cofactor, and a signature is verified without it (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.7)
R of mixed order (rB plus a point of order 8) with S = r + k·a: the equation holds only with the cofactor (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.7)
R a point of order 8 with S = k·a: the equation holds only with the cofactor; R of small order is rejected as well, so g47 is the case for the equation alone (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.7)
R the identity with S = k·a: the equation holds even without the cofactor, but R of small order is rejected, as some libraries do, so that verifiers agree (7.1)

the identity as a key, written with y = p + 1, and a signature R = [S]B, S of prime order: since k·A is the identity, the equation holds, and the standard libraries of some languages accept it; only the check that the key is canonically encoded rejects it, a list of small-order encodings does not (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.3)
the unused bits of the last character of the signature segment are set: decoders that ignore them read the valid signature, but a signed object has exactly one spelling (7.1, RFC 4648 section 3.5)
the unused bits of the last character of the payload segment are set, signed over the segment as written (7.1, RFC 4648 section 3.5)
the unused bits of the last character of the header segment are set, signed over the segment as written (7.1, RFC 4648 section 3.5)
the unused bits of the last character of x are set: the key is not base64url in its one spelling, so it cannot be used (7.1)
the header member alg twice, ES256 and then EdDSA, correctly signed: not I-JSON, and parsers differ on which one counts (7.1, RFC 7515 section 4, RFC 7493 section 2.3)
a kid of 64 characters from every class the pattern permits (7.1)
a kid of 65 characters, in the header and in the key set: at most 64 (7.1)
a kid with a slash, in the header and in the key set: outside the permitted characters (7.1)
two keys with the same kid, the signing key first: a key set in which a kid repeats verifies nothing, whichever key a verifier would pick (7.1, 10.2)
two keys with the same kid, the signing key second (7.1, 10.2)
an EdDSA signature of 65 octets, a valid one followed by a zero octet: a signature has exactly 64 (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.7)
the header member jwk with another key, signed by that key: a key is never taken from the signed object (7.1, RFC 7515 section 4.1.3)
a key with crv X25519 and the kid of the signature: a key for key agreement, not for EdDSA (7.1, RFC 8037 section 2)
an Ed25519 key whose x has 31 octets (7.1, RFC 8037 section 2)
an Ed25519 key whose x has 33 octets (7.1, RFC 8037 section 2)
an ES256 signature with r = 0 and s = 0, which some libraries once accepted for every message (7.1, RFC 7518 section 3.4)
an ES256 signature of 65 octets, a valid one followed by a zero octet: R and S are 32 octets each (7.1, RFC 7518 section 3.4)
an ES256 signature in DER, the form of other protocols: JWS uses R and S of 32 octets each (7.1, RFC 7518 section 3.4)
an ES256 signature whose R begins with a zero octet, written in 63 octets: R is always 32 octets (7.1, RFC 7518 section 3.4)

the signing key next to an RSA key in the same key set: a key set with a key that cannot be used verifies nothing, also where RFC 7517 section 5 lets a reader skip it, so that a household never trusts a set it cannot read in full (7.1, 10.2)
an Ed25519 key whose x encodes y = 2, for which no point exists on the curve: decoding fails (7.1, RFC 8032 section 5.1.3)
an ES256 signature whose r is the group order n, with the s of g02: r is between 1 and n − 1 (7.1, RFC 7518 section 3.4)
an ES256 signature with the r of g02 and s = 0 (7.1, RFC 7518 section 3.4)
the P-256 key of g02 with y + 1, a point that is not on the curve: the key verifies nothing, so the signature does not verify; the key set itself stays usable (7.1)
alg written eddsa, correctly signed: values are compared exactly, and only EdDSA names the algorithm (7.1, RFC 7515 section 4.1.1)
the signing key next to a key whose type is RSA, OKP appearing only under KTY: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key with a line feed in x: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a private key (d with an empty value): a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a private key (d with the value null): a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key of small order, the identity: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key of small order, order 8: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key written non-canonically, y = p + 1: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key for encryption (use enc): a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose use is null: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key that may only sign (key_ops without verify): a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose key_ops has an element that is not a string: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to an Ed25519 key whose alg is ES256: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose x has the unused bits of its last character set: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose x has 31 octets: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose x has 33 octets: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose kid has 65 characters: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose kid has a slash: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key without kid: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key whose kid is a number, not a string: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key with crv X25519, a key for key agreement: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a P-256 key without y: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key with the member x twice: the key set is not I-JSON: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to the member keys twice: the key set is not I-JSON: a key set with such a key verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to an Ed25519 key that is not a point of the curve, which verifies nothing and leaves the key set usable: the signature by the signing key verifies (7.1)
the signing key next to a P-256 key that is not a point of the curve, which verifies nothing and leaves the key set usable: the signature by the signing key verifies (7.1)
a key set of 65 537 bytes, one more than a key set may have, although its only key is the signing key and its long member is unknown: the key set verifies nothing (7.1, 10.2)
the signing key next to a key with a noncharacter (U+FDD0) in a member nobody reads: a key set is I-JSON, so it verifies nothing
the signing key names its algorithm Ed25519, the fully specified name of RFC 9864: that is the algorithm of an Ed25519 key

the signing key next to a P-256 key restricted to encryption: a key a restriction excludes makes the set verify nothing, also for a verifier without ES256, for which only the point of a P-256 key does not count
a key set of exactly 65 536 bytes, the most a key set may have
a header whose member name and value are written with escapes: names and values of the header are compared after unescaping, and the signature covers the bytes as they are
a header with its members in the other order and white space between them: only the segments have one spelling, not the JSON of the header
